quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop to rest or change drivers. Tiredness slows your thinking and reactions, which makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in work zones?

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as quickly as possible.
Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep space between your car and barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other cars. Increase your following distance and never tailgate.

questions.question: A school bus has its lights flashing and signal arm extended. What should you do?

options.text: Go slowly at 15 mph if you don't see children.
Go at normal speed, but watch for children.

questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing lights and an extended arm, you must stop completely. Stay stopped until the arm goes back and the bus moves. This applies whether you are behind the bus or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you can see less. Low visibility makes it difficult to judge how far away objects are and how fast other vehicles are going. You can only see as far as your headlights reach.

questions.question: A pedestrian crosses after the "Don't Walk" signal starts flashing. They are in the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Go because you have the right-of-way.
Go if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before going.
questions.explanation: At a green light, give the right-of-way to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection. If a pedestrian is crossing, wait until they finish before moving forward.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that tells drivers what they must do or not do. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street. What should you do?

options.text: Only give them the right-of-way at corners.

questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must always give the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This warning sign alerts you that the road has curves ahead.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing your lane, but there is no crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass them.
Slow down as you pass them.
Stop and let them finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them finish crossing.
questions.explanation: At intersections without traffic lights, give the right-of-way to pedestrians in any crosswalk, marked or not. Always yield to pedestrians, even without a marked crosswalk.

questions.question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light favors the pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what the situation is.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to stop if a train is near.
Find a way around any lowered gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is near.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs alert you that a train might be coming. Obey all warning signs and never drive around barriers or ignore activated signals.

questions.question: What do red or yellow painted curbs mean?
questions.explanation: Painted curbs show parking restrictions. A red curb is a fire lane. A yellow curb may be a loading zone or other parking restriction.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your body?
questions.explanation: Alcohol works quickly but leaves your body slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower blood alcohol content. Only time removes alcohol from your system.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow sign with black markings warns drivers about a steep hill. You should slow down to avoid losing control and damaging your brakes.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a car with airbags?

options.text: The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: Airbags can hurt children. All children age 12 and under must sit in the back seat.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Right turns allowed on red light.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. It is against the law.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Stay calm and focus on driving.
Drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and focus on driving.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and focus on your driving. Don't take other drivers' actions personally. Drive at the speed limit and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do if your car breaks down?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Get your car off the road and away from traffic. Turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see you.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter an aggressive driver?
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to let aggressive drivers pass. Do not compete with other drivers.

questions.question: What happens if you refuse an alcohol test?

options.text: You are exercising your right as a driver.

questions.explanation: By law, you must take an alcohol test if a police officer asks. Refusing the test can result in losing your driver license.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk and keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up to leave the area quickly.

questions.explanation: Slow down when you see pedestrians. Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What should you do before starting the car?

options.text: Make sure all passengers buckle their seat belts.

questions.explanation: Before you start the car, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs.

questions.question: Is wearing a seat belt in the front passenger seat required in Arkansas?
questions.explanation: In Arkansas, it is illegal to drive or sit in the front seat without a seat belt. Always wear your seat belt in any moving vehicle.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell you?

options.text: It is not safe to pass another car here.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass another car here.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass in a "No passing zone." These areas have poor visibility and passing would be unsafe.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive while taking medication that makes driving unsafe?

options.text: Yes, if you don't feel drowsy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance that affects your ability to drive safely. This includes prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, alcohol, and illegal drugs.
